note: Idea Library themes. Order is display order: the 42 outward themes, the seven INSIDE THE CHURCH themes, then the eight Adventist department themes. 'not' = [what belongs elsewhere, the theme it belongs to]; file it there and cross-list with also:["<this theme>"]. 'tags' = profile() need tags the theme most relates to (a default for writers, not a rule). 'digitalMin' = ideas with a digital/social component the validator requires (default 12). Synonyms are lowercase; search folds accents, so 'oracion' finds 'oración'. 'inside': true marks the eleven themes whose ideas serve the church family itself (members, officers, classes, the church's own children and youth); they follow WRITERS.md, INSIDE THE CHURCH, and need at least 10 digital ideas (digitalMin 10). 'inside': false marks department themes that serve both the church and the town (Pathfinders, Adventurers, interests, religious liberty); a theme without 'inside' is outward. An idea's 'reach' (in, out or both) defaults to 'in' in an inside theme and 'out' elsewhere (SCHEMA.md).

themes.scope: Praying for and with neighbors where they are: prayer walks and door cards, request lines, texts and ads, prayer stations in public places with permission, praying for the town, its workers and its schools in general terms.
not: vigils after a local disaster or tragedy
prayer that grows into a Bible study
serving a school's staff at its invitation

themes.es: Dar de comer a quien tiene hambre
themes.scope: Getting good food to people who are short of it: pantries and mobile pantries, free meals, grocery delivery, gleaning and gardens that feed people, SNAP and WIC help, filling school-holiday gaps, with dignity and food safety.
not: cooking and nutrition classes whose point is health
meals and kits for people living on the street
holiday dinners whose point is the season
gardens whose point is caring for creation
feeding after a flood or fire

themes.es: Personas sin hogar y vivienda insegura
themes.scope: People sleeping outside, in cars, in shelters or doubled up, and families one rent payment from eviction: presence and friendship, practical kits, showers and laundry, eviction prevention and housing navigation with partner agencies.
not: clothing closets and coat drives for everyone
housing for people coming home from prison

themes.scope: Children up to about 12, always through their parents or a programme parents choose: parent-chosen clubs (Adventurers, younger Pathfinders), family-attended events, story and play with parents present, and meeting the needs parents themselves name.
not: children with disabilities and their caregivers
the Adventurer Club itself: its levels, awards and club meetings
the church's own children's Sabbath School divisions

themes.scope: Teenagers 13 to 18, through their parents, schools that invite the church, or programmes they choose: Pathfinders, youth-led service, first jobs and skills, safe evenings run by screened adults, mentoring with parental consent.
not: sport and outdoor trips for all ages
the Pathfinder Club itself: Investiture Achievement, honors, drill, camporees
the church's own teens: AY programmes and youth-led Sabbaths

themes.scope: People about 18 to 35: students, apprentices, young workers and couples without children; campus life, first-apartment life, loneliness in a new town, honest faith questions.
not: mental health and isolation at any age

themes.es: Adultos mayores y personas confinadas en casa
themes.scope: Older neighbors and the homebound or hospitalized: visiting, phone and video calls, errands and chores, technology help, friendship across generations, care homes, and support for family caregivers.

Whole households and the parents who raise them: parenting skills, family nights, new babies, screens and sleep, grandparents raising grandchildren, family worship at home, serving the needs parents themselves name.

Couples, engaged and dating adults, and healthy relationships: enrichment, date nights, pre-marriage mentoring, communication and conflict skills, reconciliation, with licensed counselors for serious trouble.
Households led by one parent: time, money and rest; car care, childcare swaps, meals, a night off, help with paperwork and practical tasks, friendship without judgement.
not: job hunting and budgeting for everyone

themes.scope: Whole-person health the Adventist way (NEWSTART, the eight natural remedies): plant-based cooking, exercise, screenings with a referral pathway, sleep, quitting smoking, diabetes and heart health, clinics run by licensed professionals.
not: food for people who are short of it
sport and outdoor recreation for fun

themes.scope: Stress, anxiety, depression, burnout and loneliness at any age: friendship and connection, mental-health first aid, peer support with trained facilitators, and referral to professionals, never therapy by amateurs.

Alcohol, drugs, nicotine, gambling, pornography and other compulsions: hosting and supporting recovery groups (Adventist Recovery Ministries, twelve-step), families of people who use, naloxone training, sober friendship, always with professional partners.
The death of a loved one, miscarriage and infant loss, suicide loss, pet loss and other losses: presence, practical help, grief groups with trained facilitators, remembrance and memorial events.
not: community response to a disaster or tragedy

themes.scope: Newcomers to the country: English classes and conversation, paperwork help, citizenship study, legal-aid referral, refugee resettlement support, worship and welcome in heart languages, and never a question about status.
not: people who moved here from elsewhere in the U.S.

themes.scope: Finding and keeping work, starting small businesses, budgeting, debt, saving, taxes with certified preparers, scams and benefits, practical and without judgement.
Learning for all ages outside the school's own walls: homework help, reading, adult literacy, GED, digital skills, study spaces, lending libraries, with screened adults for anyone under 18.
not: serving a school, its staff and families at the school's invitation
English for speakers of other languages

themes.en: Prison, re-entry & families of the incarcerated
themes.es: Cárcel, reinserción y familias de personas encarceladas
themes.scope: People in jail or prison, returning citizens, and the families left behind: chaplaincy through the facility's own programme, letters and Bible correspondence, re-entry mentoring, jobs and housing through partners, support for prisoners' spouses and children through the caregiver.

Veterans, service members, reservists and their families: welcome and thanks, deployment support for spouses and children through the family, VA navigation through accredited partners, moral injury and PTSD support with professionals.

People with physical, sensory, intellectual and developmental disabilities and their caregivers: accessibility, respite nights, sensory-friendly events, sign language, adaptive recreation, inclusion in worship and friendship.
Women of every age and stage: friendship and mentoring, skills and health, moms' groups, Bible study, safety and dignity; Women's Ministries and Dorcas opened to the neighborhood.
Men of every age: friendship built shoulder to shoulder (projects, breakfasts, sport, fixing things), fatherhood, mentoring, health, work stress, and honest faith conversation.

One-to-one and small-circle sharing of faith once there is friendship: Bible studies at kitchen tables and online, Steps to Christ, honest answers to questions, baptism classes, lay witnessing, invitation without pressure.
not: ongoing home groups and house churches
the interest list and follow-up of people who asked for studies

themes.scope: Advertised series and public events that open the Bible: prophecy and Revelation seminars, Daniel and Revelation, health-to-hope series, archaeology nights, online series, evangelistic concerts; well planned, honestly advertised, followed up.
not: health seminars whose content is health
concerts given as a gift with no message
following up interests after a series, and the way to baptism

themes.es: Hospitalidad y bienvenida a las visitas
themes.scope: What happens when a guest arrives and afterwards: greeting, fellowship meals, first-visit follow-up, the online front door (Google profile, website, livestream chat), clear signs and access, opening homes and tables.
not: welcoming people who just moved into the area

themes.es: Vecinos nuevos y vida de barrio
themes.scope: The streets, apartment complexes and developments around the church: welcoming people who just moved in, block parties, street group chats, little free libraries, being a good neighbor on Nextdoor, belonging where people live.
Music, visual art, drama, film, crafts and creative writing given to the town and used as doors to friendship: lessons, concerts, choirs, art classes, public art, open-mic nights.
not: evangelistic concerts within a seminar series
holiday carolling as a seasonal event
music in the church's own worship services

themes.scope: Play and nature for all ages: walking, running, hiking and cycling clubs, pickup games, leagues outside Sabbath hours, camping, nature study, fishing, disc golf, adaptive recreation; friendship through movement.

Everyday practical needs other than food, housing and rides: clothing closets, coats and shoes, laundry, diapers, hygiene and period products, home repairs, yard help, repair cafés, tool libraries, furniture and appliances.

Before, during and after floods, fires, storms, heat waves, power cuts and local tragedies: preparedness teaching, checking on vulnerable neighbors, Adventist Community Services Disaster Response, cooling and warming centers, long-term recovery.

themes.es: Cuidado de la creación y limpieza del vecindario
themes.scope: Caring for God's world where we live: litter pick-ups, adopting a road or park, tree planting, pollinator and community gardens, recycling and repair, creeks and trails, nature on Sabbath afternoons.
not: gardens whose point is feeding the hungry

themes.scope: Being present and useful where neighbors spend hours every day: social media, town Facebook groups and Nextdoor, short video, livestreams, podcasts, the website and Google Business Profile, online Bible studies, text lines; honest, private and kind.

Printed and digital books and magazines with health, family and hope content: racks where people wait, Steps to Christ, student literature evangelism, magazines in waiting rooms, little free libraries, e-books and audiobooks by QR code.

themes.es: Servicio a escuelas y maestros locales
themes.scope: Public, charter and private schools as institutions, at their invitation: thanking teachers and staff, supplies through the school office, volunteering where the school asks, help with events and grounds, praying for schools among our own members in general terms.
not: tutoring and homework help run by the church

themes.en: First responders, health workers & public servants
themes.es: Personal de emergencias, de salud y servidores públicos
themes.scope: Police, firefighters, EMS, dispatchers, nurses, aides, hospital and nursing-home staff, sanitation crews, mail carriers and town employees: appreciation, meals on long shifts, chaplaincy through official programmes, support for their families, prayer.

themes.es: Hogares de acogida, adopción y niños vulnerables
themes.scope: Foster, kinship and adoptive families and the agencies that serve them: wraparound care teams, respite through licensed channels, supplies for caseworkers, recruiting foster families, supporting youth aging out, always through the agency and the caregivers.

themes.es: Sobrevivientes de abuso y violencia doméstica (con profesionales)
themes.scope: Standing with survivors of domestic violence, sexual abuse, elder abuse and trafficking through professional partners (shelters, hotlines, advocates): awareness (enditnow), safe practical help, supplies for shelters, training members to respond well; never counselling or investigating ourselves.

Getting people where they need to go: rides to appointments, groceries and church, car-care clinics, bikes for commuters, help with transit, driving practice and license tests, delivery for the homebound.

themes.es: Días festivos y estaciones del año
themes.scope: The calendar moments the whole town already keeps (New Year, Valentine's, Easter, Mother's and Father's Day, the Fourth of July, back to school, Thanksgiving, Christmas) and the seasons themselves: gifts, gatherings and quiet kindnesses.

themes.es: Grupos pequeños e iglesias en los hogares
themes.scope: Gatherings of 4 to 15 that meet in homes, workplaces, parks, cafés and online: interest-based groups, study circles, house churches and new groups, supper groups; belonging before believing.
not: support groups for a particular struggle

themes.scope: Sharing the gift of rest with a tired culture: Sabbath-afternoon nature walks, open Friday-evening suppers, rest retreats for exhausted parents and workers, screen-free days, teaching and modelling a weekly day of rest.

themes.es: Lugares de trabajo y gente de negocios
themes.scope: Where neighbors spend most waking hours: members' own workplaces with permission, shift workers, small-business owners, office and industrial parks, the chamber of commerce, chaplaincy through official channels, business mentoring.
not: members' Sabbath accommodation and religious rights at work

themes.scope: Noticing when a member is missing and following up with love: a card, call or text that says we missed you; a private care list kept by a small trusted team, with consent; birthdays and anniversaries; visits to our own sick and hospitalized members; meal trains; members who are shut in; members in crisis; a care friend for each new member; gently reconnecting with former members.
not: greeting first-time guests and their first-visit follow-up
visiting older neighbors, care homes and patients in the community
an elder's spiritual shepherding, Bible study and baptism preparation
rides, repairs and the benevolence fund run by the deacons
a Sabbath School class looking after its own members
reclaiming: Bible studies and a way back for former members who ask

themes.scope: The elders' shepherding of the church family: each elder caring for a short list of member households, visits by appointment, praying with members and anointing the sick, Bible study with new members, the elders' part in preparing candidates for baptism and nurture through the first year after baptism, encouraging family worship, spiritual mentoring, and confidential listening that refers to professionals when needed.
not: Bible studies with neighbors and friends who are not yet members
noticing absence and practical care for members
family worship and parenting for families in the community
prayer ministries, prayer chains and prayer walks
help for depression, anxiety or trauma, through professionals
Sabbath School classes and teacher training
the interest list, Bible studies with interests and the way to baptism, run by the evangelism team

themes.scope: The practical ministry of deacons and deaconesses: communion and the ordinance of humility (foot-washing) prepared with beauty and care, baptism-day care, ushering and a kind, trained safety team, the building itself as hospitality (clean, warm, accessible, well lit), a benevolence fund that protects dignity, and practical help for members such as rides and small repairs.
not: greeting guests at the door and first-visit follow-up
home repairs and practical help for neighbors in the community
rides for neighbors in the community
sign language, sensory-friendly worship and disability inclusion
baptism preparation and nurture of new believers
the church budget, treasury and giving
noticing absent members and following up

themes.scope: Faithful, joyful stewardship inside the church: treasurer's reports members can understand, online giving, tithe and offerings handled as the Church Manual directs, budgeting and debt help for members, thanking givers without ever naming amounts, generosity stories, and the stewardship of time and talents; never pressure, and never publishing who gives what.
not: money, budgeting and debt classes open to the community
the deacons' benevolence fund for members in need
serving with time and gifts in a church role

themes.scope: Helping every member find a place to serve: a nominating committee that works with prayer and care, gifts-based nominations that use the Spiritual Gifts results, a ministry fair, shadowing before serving, onboarding and training new officers, rotating roles to prevent burnout, thanking volunteers, and helping new members find their place.
not: youth leadership in the Pathfinder Club (Teen Leadership Training)
friendship and social events that weave new members in

themes.scope: The adult Sabbath School and Bible classes as a caring family: class care groups where each class looks after its own members and follows up absence, teacher training, better discussion, a class for seekers, an online class with a phone dial-in for shut-ins, a class in Spanish or another heart language, and fellowship after class.
not: children's clubs and community programs such as VBS
the youth class and AY programmes
the elders' shepherding of member households
the children's divisions, from Babies and Beginner to Teen
the mission story and the mission offerings

es: guía de estudio de la biblia

themes.es: Familia de la iglesia y compañerismo
themes.scope: The church as a family: potlucks reimagined, pairing generations, celebrating milestones together, church family nights, reconciliation when there is conflict, camping and nature days as a congregation, and weaving new members into real friendships.
not: welcoming guests, including the meal after their first visit
recreation and sports open to the community
cards and calls for each member's birthday or illness
holiday events for the whole town
abuse, which is never a matter for reconciliation

es: noche de la familia de la iglesia

themes.scope: The church's own worship, planned as a whole: the Sabbath worship service and its order, congregational singing, choirs, praise teams and accompanists, special music, the platform, the children's story, testimony time and prayer in worship, worship every member can join (large print, hearing help, seating, a quiet room), and training new musicians and worship leaders.
not: concerts, lessons and choirs given to the town
preparing communion, foot-washing and baptism day
the livestream and online church for neighbors
disability ministry for families in the community

themes.es: Escuela Sabática y ministerio de los niños
themes.scope: The church's own children, from birth through age 14 (the Church Manual's span for children's ministries): the children's Sabbath School divisions from Babies and Beginner to Teen, their leaders and teachers, children's church and the children's part of worship, children's choirs, planning and staffing the church's Vacation Bible School, faith at home for the church's families, and the safe-church rules that protect every child: screened adults, the two-adult rule, check-in and check-out to parents.
not: clubs, story hours, VBS invitations and events for neighbors' children
the Adventurer Club, ages 4 to 9 with their parents
the youth Sabbath School class after Teen, and AY
parenting support for families in the community
children with disabilities and their families, as outreach

themes.scope: The church's Pathfinder Club for ages 10 to 15 (grades 5 to 8 in the North American Division, with Teen Leadership Training for high-schoolers): the Investiture Achievement levels from Friend to Guide, honors, drill and marching, campouts and camporees, Pathfinder Bible Experience, Investiture and World Pathfinder Day, the staff and counselors who run it, service the club gives the town, and neighbors' children who join through their parents.
not: teen programmes the club does not run
the church's own teens in AY and youth-led Sabbaths
hiking, camping and sport open to all ages
clean-ups the whole church does for the town

themes.scope: The church's Adventurer Club for children ages 4 to 9 (pre-kindergarten to grade 4) together with their parents: the six levels from Little Lamb to Helping Hand, stars, chips and awards, family-centered meetings built on My God, My Self, My Family and My World, Investiture, the Family Network that supports parents from the church and the community, and neighbor families who join through the parents.
not: story hours, VBS and events for neighbors' children
parenting classes open to the community

themes.scope: The church's own teens and youth, about 13 to 18 (Adventist Youth Ministries in the Church Manual): youth-led Sabbaths and AY programmes, vespers, the youth Sabbath School class, mentoring with parental consent, Youth Week of Prayer and Global Youth Day service, a youth council that gives teens a real voice, and youth mission trips done well; always with screened adults, the two-adult rule and parental consent.
not: teens in the community: programmes they choose, first jobs, safe evenings
short-term mission trips for all ages

themes.es: Seguimiento de interesados y nuevos creyentes
themes.scope: Caring for the people who have asked to know more, until they are at home in the church family: the interest list kept kindly and privately by the interest coordinator, prompt follow-up of requests from a series, a Bible school, a card or a media ministry, Bible studies with interests by members and Bible workers, the way to baptism, welcoming each new member on baptism day and handing them on to an elder and a care friend, and reclaiming former members who ask to come back.
not: friendship evangelism and studies members start with their own friends
an elder's nurture of new members through their first year
a yearly card and a homecoming invitation that ask nothing of former members
online Bible studies and digital evangelism

themes.scope: Freedom of conscience for everyone, as the Public Affairs and Religious Liberty (PARL) department teaches: helping members keep the Sabbath at work (knowing their rights, asking for accommodation well, calling the conference PARL director early), Religious Liberty Sabbath and Liberty magazine, respectful community forums on freedom of conscience for people of every faith and none, and standing with neighbors of other faiths when their freedom is threatened; never partisan politics.
not: serving members and neighbors at their workplaces
the Sabbath as a gift of rest

themes.scope: The world church's mission, brought home: mission stories told well in Sabbath School and worship, the Thirteenth Sabbath Offering and the other mission offerings explained and passed on in full, praying for and supporting Global Mission pioneers, Mission Spotlight videos, members and missionaries serving abroad, and short-term mission trips done well: invited by the church there, serving under local leaders, never tourism and never photos of poverty.
not: youth mission trips planned by the AY
